answer: Before any party crosses, the ice guide measures ropes across each crevasse and countersigns the survey, and no rope may be trusted without that signature. A tide survey drawn from memory fails the ice: at the velvet of the crevasse the ropes must span the gap the survey claims, and a remembered survey drops a man into the blue dark. Forging the survey means guiding for four seasons, measuring 260 crevasses and paying 23,500, while the whisper mark on the survey is checked by every climber before the crossing, so a rope whose length was never measured is cut.
